contentBlocks.text: ਹੁਣ ਉਲਟ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ! (Now the opposite direction!) Translating Punjabi to English requires re-ordering words back into Subject-Verb-Object.

Translating from Punjabi to English means reversing yesterday's process: read the Punjabi Subject-Object-Verb sentence, identify each word's meaning, then reorder into English Subject-Verb-Object. Translate: ਛੋਟੀ ਕੁੜੀ ਦੁੱਧ ਪੀਂਦੀ ਹੈ (ਛੋਟੀ = small, ਕੁੜੀ = girl, ਦੁੱਧ = milk, ਪੀਂਦੀ ਹੈ = drinks). Identify each word's meaning first, then write the correctly reordered English sentence.
You just translated a real sentence from Punjabi back into natural English. Tomorrow we'll translate a short paragraph, combining both directions.

objectives: Translate a Punjabi sentence into natural English
Correctly reverse Subject-Object-Verb order into Subject-Verb-Object for English
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's English-to-Punjabi translation.
2. Work through the ਛੋਟੀ ਕੁੜੀ ਦੁੱਧ ਪੀਂਦੀ ਹੈ example together.
3. Have the child translate one more Punjabi sentence independently.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: translating a full paragraph.
differentiationTips: Struggling: have the child identify each word's meaning first (writing English under each Punjabi word) before attempting to reorder into a sentence
Ready for more: ask them to translate a sentence with an adjective describing the object too, not just the subject
All Gurmukhi words/sentences used in this lesson were validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. ਛੋਟੀ ਕੁੜੀ ਦੁੱਧ ਪੀਂਦੀ ਹੈ। = The small girl drinks milk. 2. ਵੱਡਾ ਮੁੰਡਾ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਪੜ੍ਹਦਾ ਹੈ। = The big boy reads a book.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Completes the two-directional translation skill (English-to-Punjabi from Day 2, Punjabi-to-English here), addressing the course's 'translation practice' description from both directions before Day 4's paragraph-level synthesis.

generationData.instructions: Translate each Punjabi sentence into English.
